newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude flat with NYMEX amid thin talk.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude flat with NYMEX amid thin talk.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices eased Wednesday, with local trade quiet as traders did paperwork or attended an industry function, dealers said.
Refiners said the hoped to buy benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) grade at prices well below the discount of $1.75 off July West Texas Intermediate, done May 23.
"ANS is weaker than the numbers indicate," one trader said.
Late Tuesday, the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported crude oil inventories in the West Coast region rose 311,000 barrels last week, a negligible number, according to local traders.
Buyers scoffed at the offer made by ANS's largest producer, a discount of $1.60.
No trades have transpired this week with many refiners at a rafting trip sponsored by Tosco Corp Monday and Tuesday.
Traders heard rumors that ANS' largest seller has diverted supplies west in an attempt to clear out inventories.
The producer allegedly sold a pipeline cargo of ANS to a Midwest refinery at $2.00 under July WTI, the equivalent of $4.00 under into the West Coast, traders said.
